group.passage: Why have allergies become so common? In the two texts below, a science writer looks back at one famous explanation, and a doctor at a children’s allergy clinic explains why she worries about the way it is often understood.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: A Theory from Big Families
passage_parts.text: Allergies such as hay fever and asthma have become far more common in the developed world over recent decades. In 1989, a British doctor, David Strachan, studied records of thousands of children born in 1958 and noticed something unexpected: hay fever was less common among those with several older brothers and sisters. He suggested that the infections passed around in large families might train a young immune system to tell real threats apart from harmless things such as pollen. As families got smaller and homes cleaner, fewer children would receive this early training. His idea came to be called the “hygiene hypothesis.” Later studies gave the idea a twist. Children raised on traditional farms, in daily contact with cows and barn dust, turned out to have far less asthma than other children, even those on modern farms. Today many researchers believe that what protects us is not the germs that make us sick but everyday contact with harmless microbes from soil, animals and other people. Many also believe that these tiny living things do the most good when they are as diverse as possible.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Keep Washing Those Hands
passage_parts.text: As a doctor at a children’s allergy clinic, I can confirm that the rise in allergies is real: I see far more young patients with asthma and hay fever today than when I started out. What worries me is the theory’s name. Because of the word “hygiene,” many parents now lay the blame on soap and water, and some have even given up washing their children’s hands. Yet researchers moved on from Strachan’s focus on infections long ago; only the old name has stuck. Handwashing removes the germs that cause serious illness, but it does very little to the friendly microbes we pick up outdoors, from food and from other people. So keep washing hands before meals and after using the toilet, and also let children dig in the garden and play with animals. Finally, remember that allergies have many causes, from the genes we inherit to the air we breathe and the food we eat. As for which of these matters most, the jury is still out.

questions.stem: Which phrase does the doctor in Text B use to say that a question “has not yet been settled”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: Text A 最後說，許多研究者認為保護我們的不是讓人生病的病菌，而是日常接觸無害的微生物，而且這些微小生物越多樣（diverse）效果越好。摘要句「保護孩子的似乎不是感染，而是周遭無害微生物的＿＿」中，空格在 the 之後、of 之前，要填名詞；把形容詞 diverse 改成名詞 diversity（多樣性）。
evidence: Today many researchers believe that what protects us is not the germs that make us sick but everyday contact with harmless microbes from soil, animals and other people.
Many also believe that these tiny living things do the most good when they are as diverse as possible.

把形容詞 diverse 改成名詞。

2.explanation_zh: Text B 的醫師說，因為「衛生」這個詞，許多父母現在把過敏的責任（the blame）推給肥皂和清水，有些人甚至不再幫孩子洗手；她接著說明洗手去除的是致病的病菌，對友善的微生物幾乎沒有影響。摘要句 has been unfairly ___ for causing allergies 是現在完成式被動語態，要填過去分詞；把名詞 blame 轉成動詞（責怪、歸咎），再變成過去分詞 blamed：「日常洗手被不公平地歸咎為造成過敏的原因」（blame A for B：把 B 歸咎於 A）。

hints: has been ___ for causing：被動語態，要過去分詞，並且能接 for＋V-ing。
Text B 說父母因為「衛生」這個詞，把過敏怪到什麼東西頭上？用的是哪個名詞？
把名詞 blame 當動詞用，再改成過去分詞。

3.explanation_zh: 題目要選兩篇都支持的敘述。(B) Text A 第一句說過敏在已開發國家近幾十年變得常見許多；Text B 醫師說過敏增加是真的，她現在看到的過敏病童比剛執業時多得多，兩篇都明說。(D) Text A 說後來的研究讓這個想法有了轉折，現在許多研究者認為重點不是讓人生病的病菌；Text B 說研究者早就不再把重點放在史特拉肯所說的感染，只剩舊名稱留下來，可推知兩篇都認為原本的理論已被後來的研究修正。(G) Text A 把「讓人生病的病菌」和「無害的微生物」對比；Text B 把「造成嚴重疾病的病菌」和「友善的微生物」對比，可推知兩篇都認為微生物對健康的影響不一樣。其餘：(A) 只有 Text A 提到哥哥姊姊；(F) 只有 Text B 批評名稱；(C) 兩篇都說研究的重點已經不是感染；(E) 看似是「衛生假說」的意思，但 Text B 說把責任推給肥皂和清水是誤解，過敏有許多成因，Text A 也只說這是史特拉肯當初的推想；(H) 與 Text B 要大家繼續洗手的建議矛盾。

As a doctor at a children’s allergy clinic, I can confirm that the rise in allergies is real: I see far more young patients with asthma and hay fever today than when I started out.
C: Today many researchers believe that what protects us is not the germs that make us sick but everyday contact with harmless microbes from soil, animals and other people.

D: Later studies gave the idea a twist.

E: Because of the word “hygiene,” many parents now lay the blame on soap and water, and some have even given up washing their children’s hands.

F: What worries me is the theory’s name.

G: Today many researchers believe that what protects us is not the germs that make us sick but everyday contact with harmless microbes from soil, animals and other people.
Handwashing removes the germs that cause serious illness, but it does very little to the friendly microbes we pick up outdoors, from food and from other people.
H: So keep washing hands before meals and after using the toilet, and also let children dig in the garden and play with animals.

4.explanation_zh: the jury is still out 字面是「陪審團還沒有做出裁決」，引申為「還沒有定論、尚未確定」，正是題幹 has not yet been settled（還沒有解決、還沒有定論）的意思。醫師說過敏有許多成因，但哪一個最重要，目前還沒有定論。答案寫 the jury is still out，保留文中的完整說法。
evidence: As for which of these matters most, the jury is still out.
4.strategy_zh: 題幹限定說話者（Text B 的醫師），並用文中沒有的 settled 指稱概念；在她談過敏成因的最後一句找表示「尚無定論」的慣用語，只抄慣用語本身，不要連 As for which of these matters most 一起抄。

translation_zh.text:
為什麼過敏變得這麼常見？在下面兩篇短文中，一位科普作家回顧一個著名的解釋，一位兒童過敏門診的醫師則說明，她為什麼擔心大家常常誤解這個解釋。

A　來自大家庭的理論
近幾十年來，花粉熱、氣喘等過敏疾病在已開發國家變得常見許多。1989 年，英國醫師大衛．史特拉肯研究數千名 1958 年出生的兒童的紀錄，注意到一件出乎意料的事：有好幾個哥哥姊姊的孩子比較少得花粉熱。他提出，在大家庭裡互相傳染的疾病，也許能訓練年幼的免疫系統分辨真正的威脅和花粉之類無害的東西。隨著家庭變小、家裡變乾淨，得到這種早期訓練的孩子就變少了。他的想法後來被稱為「衛生假說」。後來的研究讓這個想法有了轉折：在傳統農場長大、每天接觸牛隻和穀倉塵土的孩子，得氣喘的比例遠低於其他孩子，即使和住在現代化農場的孩子相比也是如此。現在許多研究者認為，保護我們的不是讓人生病的病菌，而是日常接觸來自土壤、動物和其他人的無害微生物。許多人也認為，這些微小生物越多樣，帶來的益處越大。

B　繼續洗手
身為兒童過敏門診的醫師，我可以證實過敏的增加是真的：我現在看到的氣喘和花粉熱小病人，比我剛開始執業時多得多。讓我擔心的是這個理論的名稱。因為「衛生」這個詞，許多父母現在把責任推給肥皂和清水，有些人甚至不再幫孩子洗手。然而研究者早就不再把重點放在史特拉肯所說的感染上，只有舊名稱還留著。洗手能去除造成嚴重疾病的病菌，但對我們在戶外、從食物中、從其他人身上接觸到的友善微生物幾乎沒有影響。所以飯前便後要繼續洗手，也要讓孩子在花園裡挖土、和動物玩。最後，請記得過敏有許多成因，從我們遺傳到的基因，到我們呼吸的空氣和吃的食物都是。至於其中哪一個最重要，目前還沒有定論。

He suggested that infections passed around in large families might train a young immune system, and that smaller families and cleaner homes meant fewer children received this early training.

Children raised on traditional farms, in daily contact with cows and barn dust, have far less asthma than other children, even those on modern farms (Amish vs. Hutterite).

Many researchers now believe what protects us is not the germs that make us sick but everyday contact with harmless microbes; these microbes do the most good when they are as diverse as possible (wide range of harmless microbes).
Researchers moved on from Strachan’s focus on infections long ago; only the old name has stuck.

Because of the word “hygiene,” many parents blame soap and water and some have given up washing their children’s hands (the name is misleading and can lead people to neglect hygiene; the doctor’s clinic observation is a fictional first-person framing of this fact).

Handwashing removes the germs that cause serious illness but does very little to the friendly microbes; keep washing hands before meals and after using the toilet (targeted hygiene; the advice is the writer’s commentary based on f7–f9, as the fact sheet notes).
Allergies have many causes, from the genes we inherit to the air we breathe and the food we eat; which matters most is not settled.
